content.comment_body: Hello, I have a new [product_name] module. The enclosed product information lists an IP address and default credentials: 192.168.0.3, username: admin, password: admin. I can access the web server, but I'm unable to log in—it always says login failed. Has the password or username been changed since the literature was printed?
Hi, I'm encountering the same issue.
Hello [user_name], I held the SET button for 10 seconds and that resolved the issue—I was able to log in.
I did the same, thank you.
It's beneficial to create two separate user accounts for logging into the [product_name] module during your first setup, as this could be helpful later on.
I'm also having this problem with two [product_name] modules.
The reset button needs to be pressed for exactly 10 seconds. After that, it works correctly.

Hello, this issue persists. The reset works, but the password problem remains. After setting or disabling the password and waiting offline for hours, the password still doesn't work and configuration is not possible. I've tested this with six modules and consistently have the same issue.

Hi, I still can't log in. Pressing the set button for 10 seconds puts the [product_name] module in the correct mode. After cutting and restoring power, it restarts but continues to request login credentials, and admin/admin does not work. What steps should I take now?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are consistently running into login issues when trying to access the [product_name] module web server using the default credentials. While some users temporarily resolve access problems with recommended reset steps, others report continuous difficulties with authentication, causing frustration and interfering with configuration or module usage.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the documented default login credentials for these modules to be reliable and secure, and want clear, dependable authentication procedures for both initial setup and ongoing configuration. They also desire straightforward guidance and consistent access after performing resets.
